newsitem.title: USA: Ball to sell glass unit stake for $190 million.
newsitem.headline: Ball to sell glass unit stake for $190 million.

text.p: Ball Corp. said Monday it will sell its 42 percent interest in Ball-Foster Glass Container Co. L.L.C. to its partner in the joint venture, French glassmaker Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, for about $190 million.
Ball, which makes metal and plastic packaging mainly for foods and beverages, said it will record a gain on the sale, but did not specify the amount.
The definitive agreement is expected to close before the end of the year, subject to regulatory filings.
Ball said the companies set up Ball-Foster in 1995 to acquire the glass manufacturing operations of both Ball Glass Container Corp. and Foster-Forbes, then a unit of Pechiney SA.
Ball retained a 42 percent interest in Ball-Foster through two units, while Saint-Gobain received the other 58 percent.
Under the agreement creating Ball-Foster, Ball's glass subsidiaries had a right to put their interest in Ball-Foster to Saint-Gobain on a formula basis beginning in 1998.
Saint-Gobain said the acquisition will have a positive impact on its net result from 1997.

Ball, which also provides aerospace and other technologies to government and commercial customers, added that its third-quarter results from continuing operations likely will not exceed year-ago results, as it had previously expected.
In the 1995 third quarter, Muncie, Ind.-based Ball reported a loss of $57.3 million, or $1.92 a share, on revenues of $760.7 million, after charges related to the sale of its glass business.
Ball attributed its outlook largely to lower than anticipated beverage cans shipments, a drop in aluminum prices, and lower food can shipments.

"In addition to the pressures on our North American can businesses, somewhat higher costs associated with startups in our new plastic container business and with our new international can manufacturing joint ventures are having a negative impact on our third quarter," the company said.
Ball said it opened three new can plants in China in recent months, has beverage can plants under construction in Brazil and Thailand, and is building a fourth plastic container plant in Ames, Iowa.
Ball's stock fell 37.5 cents to $24.375 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
